grades.quote: |3|17|DBAR_hints|1 indicates that the non-0 value of the DBAR is implemented according to the recommended meaning of the manual.|
grades.reason: This CPUCFG table has a DBAR_hints bit saying whether non-zero DBAR hint values follow the manual's recommended meaning. That is peripheral to DBAR 0 and does not state what ordering DBAR 0 guarantees.

grades.quote: Before any synchronization operation is allowed to be executed, all ordinary memory access operations that precede this synchronization operation in the same processor have been completed.
grades.reason: This passage gives LoongArch's weak consistency model. It names DBAR as a synchronization operation and states the ordering rules for synchronization operations against ordinary memory accesses. That is the basis for what a full DBAR 0 barrier enforces. It never mentions the hint value 0 explicitly.
This passage covers RISC-V FENCE and RVWMO I/O ordering, which is the wrong ISA for a question about LoongArch DBAR 0.
